summary: The machine has the Python runtime, the DocumentDB data-plane MCP server, the Azure MCP server and the Microsoft Learn documentation MCP server, plus a full set of DocumentDB agent skills required to build the sample app. The build can start now against the provided cluster (DOCUMENTDB_URI). Important cold-answer misconceptions were found (resource type, CLI group, billing model, authentication, vector/search support, local dev image, change streams) and corrected with Microsoft docs; they must be applied by the builder. Missing accelerators and a few local CLI tools (azd, bicep, terraform, mongosh, dotnet) are not blocking but would speed development or IaC work if added.
summary_points: Build can start: python + pip are available and the documentdb MCP server is present for verification; the provided cluster URI pattern (DOCUMENTDB_URI) and database name are usable now.

Key model-memory errors (cold answers) must be corrected: the cluster resource is Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (not databaseAccounts), the CLI group is az documentdb mongocluster, and billing is compute (vCore tiers) + storage (not RU/s).

Azure DocumentDB supports Microsoft Entra ID (MONGODB-OIDC) and native vector indexes (DiskANN, HNSW, IVF) and integrated full-text/vector/hybrid search via cosmosSearch; change streams are supported.
Local development uses the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image (Mongo on port 10260 with TLS and SCRAM-SHA-256), not the Cosmos DB Emulator; the documentdb-local-deployment skill documents this.
Accelerators missing but useful: DocumentDB Agent Kit (npx skills add ...) and IaC CLIs (bicep/terraform) — helpful but not required for the sample.
No unavailable required tool blocks the build, but some factual corrections and README/seed choices must be applied before publishing the sample.

tools.name: python
tools.needed_for: Run the sample, virtualenv, pip install, run seed and pipeline scripts.
tools.detail: Python 3.13.13 on PATH (virtualenv expected per skill_md).
tools.impact_if_missing: Sample cannot run or be developed in Python.

tools.name: pip
tools.needed_for: Install sample dependencies and packages (pymongo, langchain, embeddings/LLM SDKs).
tools.workaround: Use system package manager to install packages or vendor dependencies in repo.

tools.name: documentdb (MCP server)
tools.needed_for: Data-plane verification: list databases, create collections and indexes, run aggregation and $search queries, sample documents, explain plans and verify what the sample created.
tools.detail: documentdb MCP server present with 18 data-plane tools (documentdb_list_databases, documentdb_create_index, documentdb_aggregate, etc.).
tools.impact_if_missing: Would lose programmatic verification of collections/indexes and query explanations; developer would have to rely on manual portal checks.
tools.workaround: Use the Azure portal and az CLI to inspect resources, or install the documentdb MCP toolkit. For local tests, use the Gateway Docker image.

tools.name: learn (Microsoft Learn docs MCP server)
tools.needed_for: Grounding documentation and authoritative references (index creation patterns, auth methods, vector search docs used for correctness).
tools.detail: learn_microsoft_docs_search and documentation fetch tools available.
tools.impact_if_missing: Harder to quickly verify current recommendations and examples; agent would need web access to docs.
tools.workaround: Rely on installed documentdb-* skills' internal docs; or developers consult learn.microsoft.com manually.

tools.name: azure (MCP server)
tools.needed_for: Control-plane lookups and guidance (az CLI mapping, best practice lookups). Helpful for optional IaC verification and management-plane checks.
tools.impact_if_missing: Less convenient control-plane guidance; az CLI can still be used for queries.
tools.workaround: Use az CLI directly and Microsoft Learn pages for control-plane docs.

tools.name: az (Azure CLI)
tools.needed_for: Inspect subscription and resource groups, optional IaC or portal-equivalent checks; useful to retrieve resource details and connection strings when permitted.
tools.detail: Azure CLI 2.89.1 and cosmosdb-preview extension present per inventory.
tools.impact_if_missing: Slower control-plane operations; cannot script resource queries.
tools.workaround: Use Azure Portal for resource inspection or REST APIs via curl.

tools.name: docker
tools.needed_for: Optional local DocumentDB Gateway image for local integration tests (recommended by documentdb-local-deployment skill).
tools.detail: Docker available but no local gateway running.
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot run local Gateway-based integration tests; must test against live cluster.
tools.workaround: Run tests against the live cluster (DOCUMENTDB_URI) as described in skill_md. Use seeded test data and mock LLMs for unit tests.

tools.name: node / npx
tools.needed_for: Installing agent skills (accelerators) or starting some MCP-related developer tooling; optional for DocumentDB Agent Kit installation.
tools.impact_if_missing: Harder to quickly add skills via npx; non-blocking for Python sample.
tools.workaround: Install skills manually or copy required assets into the repo.

tools.name: mongosh
tools.needed_for: Manual interactive checks against Mongo wire protocol endpoints and local gateway (hand-run queries).
tools.detail: mongosh not found on PATH per inventory.
tools.impact_if_missing: Less convenient to run ad-hoc manual queries by hand; still possible via pymongo scripts or documentdb MCP server.
tools.workaround: Use the documentdb MCP server tools (documentdb_find_documents, documentdb_aggregate) or write small pymongo scripts to inspect data.

tools.name: git
tools.needed_for: Source control for the sample repository.
tools.impact_if_missing: Cannot version or share code easily.
tools.workaround: Use zip bundles or other source management.

tools.name: documentdb-driver (skill)
tools.needed_for: Driver usage guidance (singleton MongoClient, connection pooling) and sample code patterns for pymongo.
tools.impact_if_missing: Developers may misuse MongoClient patterns and cause pool exhaustion or connection inefficiencies.
tools.workaround: Follow community pymongo best practices; but having the skill is preferable.

tools.name: documentdb-local-deployment (skill)
tools.needed_for: Local dev guidance: which Docker image to run, ports (10260), TLS settings, seed data flags and dev/prod parity rules.
tools.detail: Skill loaded and documents the Gateway image and port 10260.
tools.impact_if_missing: Local dev instructions would be missing, increasing friction for offline testing.
tools.workaround: Runner can use live cluster but should adopt the skill's port/TLS conventions if later using the Gateway.

tools.name: documentdb-vector-search (skill)
tools.needed_for: Index creation, vector index type selection (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF), and tuning parameters for embeddings and vector searches.
tools.detail: Skill installed; docs and examples available.
tools.impact_if_missing: Builder may create incompatible vector indexes or mis-tune parameters (numLists, efSearch, lBuild) and waste time.
tools.workaround: Follow the Microsoft Learn vector-search docs referenced in the report.

tools.name: documentdb-indexing (skill)
tools.needed_for: Choosing appropriate single-field, compound, textSearch and vector indexes for dedupe, lookups and search.
tools.impact_if_missing: Risk of poor query performance and COLLSCAN in aggregation pipelines.
tools.workaround: Follow the vector and indexing Learn pages listed in grounding links.

tools.name: documentdb-natural-language-querying (skill)
tools.needed_for: Generating sample queries/aggregation pipelines for dedupe and enrichment read operations from natural language prompts (useful in dev and README examples).
tools.detail: Installed; requires the documentdb MCP server for sample-context generation.
tools.workaround: Author queries by hand or use community tools.

accelerators_missed: DocumentDB Agent Kit (npx skills add Azure/documentdb-agent-kit) - would speed sample scaffolding and ensure consistent patterns in code + README.

Azure DocumentDB MCP Toolkit entry in mcp.json (documentdb) - the documentdb MCP server is present, but if the agent kit accelerator variant (GitHub repo) were installed it would speed schema/index scaffolding and testing.

confusions.question: What is the Azure resource provider namespace and resource type of an Azure DocumentDB cluster?
confusions.cold_answer: Azure Cosmos DB (DocumentDB) resources live under the Microsoft.DocumentDB provider. The account resource type is: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts (child resources include Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/mongodbDatabases and Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/mongodbCollections).
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB clusters are deployed as resource type Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (not databaseAccounts).

grounding_links.title: Microsoft.DocumentDB mongoClusters 2024-07-01 (deployment-language-terraform)
Microsoft.DocumentDB mongoClusters 2025-07-01-preview (deployment-language-terraform)

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Shared provider namespace (Microsoft.DocumentDB) and historical overlap between Cosmos DB account resource names and older MongoDB API/account models; older docs and examples continue to reference databaseAccounts.
confusions.build_risk: Using databaseAccounts in Bicep/ARM/Terraform or CLI will target the older Cosmos DB account resources (RU-mode) and not create the vCore mongoClusters the sample must use; IaC and CLI scripts would fail or produce a different service.
improvements: Deprecate or add a clear banner on older Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts pages clarifying that vCore clusters are Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters and link to the new page.
Update quickstarts and code samples to show the new resource type when the sample targets vCore clusters.

confusions.question: Which Azure CLI command group creates and manages a cluster? Is it in the core CLI or an extension?
confusions.cold_answer: Use the built-in Azure CLI group az cosmosdb (core CLI). Examples: az cosmosdb create ...
confusions.grounded_answer: The current CLI command group for vCore clusters is az documentdb mongocluster (and az cosmosdb also has mongocluster commands in some CLI versions); the service exposes az documentdb mongocluster create. Use az documentdb mongocluster for the new vCore DocumentDB clusters.

grounding_links.title: az documentdb mongocluster create
az cosmosdb mongocluster create

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Older Cosmos DB/MongoDB API guidance uses az cosmosdb; the rebranded vCore offering and the newer az documentdb CLI group overlap in naming.
confusions.build_risk: Using az cosmosdb create or databaseAccounts-oriented commands may create the wrong type of account (RU-mode) or fail to expose vCore-specific parameters (tier, nodeCount) required by the sample.
improvements: Explicitly document in the Azure CLI reference which command group to use for vCore mongoClusters (az documentdb mongocluster) and add examples in the quickstarts.
Add a short migration note near az cosmosdb docs explaining the difference and pointing to az documentdb for vCore clusters.

confusions.question: Which Bicep and Terraform resource types deploy a cluster?
confusions.cold_answer: Bicep/ARM: Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts and child types; Terraform azurerm_cosmosdb_account etc.
confusions.grounded_answer: Bicep/ARM and Terraform examples for vCore clusters use Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (and corresponding AzAPI/Terraform modules/AVMs for the Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore) / DocumentDB module).

grounding_links.title: Microsoft.DocumentDB mongoClusters 2024-07-01 (deployment-language-terraform)
Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore) cluster `[Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters]` (AVM README)

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Historical use of Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts for Cosmos DB accounts (Mongo API) and overlapping terminology in IaC samples.
confusions.build_risk: Using the databaseAccounts resource in IaC will produce a RU-mode Cosmos account, not a vCore mongoClusters cluster; the cluster will have different capabilities (no vCore tiers, different index/search features).
improvements: Update IaC quickstarts and AVM module READMEs to use the mongoClusters resource for vCore clusters, and add a short note listing the differences vs databaseAccounts.

confusions.question: What does a connection string look like: scheme, host suffix, port, and the options it must carry?
confusions.cold_answer: mongodb://<username>:<password>@<account>.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?ssl=true&replicaSet=globaldb&retrywrites=false&appName=@<account>@ (port 10255, mongodb:// scheme)
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB vCore clusters use mongodb+srv (or mongodb+srv/mongodb) URIs that point at hosts like <cluster>.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com or <cluster>.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com; TLS must be enabled and recommended authMechanism is MONGODB-OIDC for Microsoft Entra ID scenarios. Use the portal/Get connection strings to copy the correct string.

grounding_links.title: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID
Get-AzDocumentDBMongoClusterConnectionString

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The mongodb:// + port 10255 pattern is the older Cosmos DB Mongo API convention; the vCore clusters use mongocluster DNS names and SRV-style URIs for multi-cluster/global endpoints.

confusion_sources.title: Typical Cosmos DB (MongoDB API) connection string examples

confusions.build_risk: Using the wrong host/port or omitting SRV/TLS settings will cause connection failures or mis-route clients (especially in multi-cluster/global scenarios).
improvements: Add an explicit example connection string for vCore clusters (mongodb+srv form with mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com) on the main quickstart and connection docs.

confusions.question: How is capacity provisioned and billed: request units, compute tiers with vCores, serverless, or something else?
confusions.cold_answer: Azure Cosmos DB bills throughput in Request Units (RU/s) and MongoDB API is RU-model (provisioned RU or autoscale).
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB (vCore) uses a compute+storage billing model: you pick a cluster tier (vCores, M10/M20/M30/etc.) and storage per shard; it is not RU-based. RU-based Cosmos DB is a different product (Cosmos DB for MongoDB RU).

grounding_links.title: Azure DocumentDB pricing explained
Azure DocumentDB pricing explained - compute cluster tiers

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Cosmos DB's long-standing RU model applies to the RU-mode Cosmos DB service; the vCore-based product has different billing and naming, which can be conflated in memory.

confusion_sources.title: Find the request unit charge for operations executed in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

confusions.build_risk: If the sample or README instructs users to provision RU throughput or explains costs in RU terms, users will provision the wrong service or be surprised by pricing.
improvements: Document the vCore pricing model clearly at top of quickstarts and in the sample README so authors do not assume RU-based billing.

confusions.question: Which authentication methods are supported, and how does a driver authenticate with Microsoft Entra ID?
confusions.cold_answer: Clients authenticate with MongoDB-style username/password (SCRAM) using account keys; Microsoft Entra ID is only management-plane and not supported for data-plane drivers.
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB supports multiple authentication modes including SCRAM (username/password) and Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) for data-plane via authMechanism=MONGODB-OIDC (role-based access). The cluster can be configured to allow MicrosoftEntraID auth modes.

grounding_links.title: Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID
az documentdb mongocluster create --auth-allowed-modes

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Earlier Cosmos Mongo API accounts historically relied on SCRAM and account keys; newer vCore DocumentDB exposes Microsoft Entra ID/OIDC options and documentation that may not have been widely known.

confusion_sources.title: Older Cosmos DB MongoDB API docs that focus on SCRAM and account keys

confusions.build_risk: If builder assumes Entra ID is not available, they might bake long-lived account keys into tests or docs instead of using role-based auth or OIDC flows.
improvements: Add a short 'Data-plane Entra ID auth' example to the quickstart showing how to set auth modes and sample mongo URI for MONGODB-OIDC.

confusions.question: Which client library should an application use? Is there a service-specific SDK?
confusions.cold_answer: Use the official MongoDB drivers (pymongo for Python); there is no special 'Cosmos DB Mongo driver'.
confusions.grounded_answer: Correct: use standard MongoDB drivers (pymongo) to talk to Azure DocumentDB clusters over the MongoDB wire protocol; management operations use Azure/DocumentDB control-plane SDKs.

grounding_links.title: What is Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)?

confusions.question: Which vector index types are supported, and what does the command that creates one look like?
confusions.cold_answer: Azure Cosmos DB's MongoDB API does not provide native vector search indexes (HNSW/IVF/DiskANN).
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB includes native vector indexes (vector-ivf, vector-hnsw, vector-diskann). Indexes are created with a createIndexes command using key: { '<path>': 'cosmosSearch' } and cosmosSearchOptions containing kind, dimensions and algorithm parameters; vector search uses the $search aggregation stage with cosmosSearch.

grounding_links.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB - Perform vector similarity search
Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB - example using an ivf index

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Many MongoDB-compatible services (including older Cosmos DB docs) do not expose built-in vector indexes; memory conflated those older constraints with the new vCore product's integrated vector search.
confusions.build_risk: If the builder assumes no native vector support, they may add a separate vector store (increasing complexity and cost) or implement an incorrect index creation flow.
improvements: Add a short 'create vector index' example snippet to the sample README demonstrating createIndexes with cosmosSearchOptions and a minimal IVF/HNSW/DiskANN example.

confusions.question: How are full-text search and hybrid search done?
confusions.cold_answer: Full-text search is done by integrating Azure Cognitive Search or external search; no integrated hybrid vector+text search is available.
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB provides integrated full-text and hybrid search via createSearchIndexes and the $search aggregation stage (cosmosSearch), supporting BM25, fuzzy, phrase search and hybrid BM25+vector retrieval via the cosmosSearch operator.

grounding_links.title: Full-text and hybrid search guidance in Azure DocumentDB
documentdb-full-text-search (skill)

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Older Cosmos DB patterns relied on Cognitive Search; the vCore product integrates text + vector search into the database engine.
confusions.build_risk: Builder might design the sample to push vectors and text to an external search service, complicating the sample and obscuring the integrated features the product provides.
improvements: Ensure quickstarts and sample READMEs demonstrate $search + cosmosSearch hybrid use-cases so authors know they can keep vectors and documents in one collection.

confusions.question: Which MongoDB wire protocol or server versions are supported, and which commonly used MongoDB features are not?
confusions.cold_answer: Cosmos DB's MongoDB API exposes several versions historically (3.2-4.2 etc); exact support depends on account config; many features differ and change streams historically not supported.
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB supports MongoDB wire protocol versions 5.0, 6.0, 7.0 and 8.0 and provides high coverage of MongoDB operators (99.03%). Some admin commands and a small set of aggregation features are managed or differ; verify specific operator coverage via the compatibility docs. Change streams are supported (see Q12).

grounding_links.title: MongoDB Query Language (MQL) compatibility in Azure DocumentDB
Azure DocumentDB at a glance - MongoDB compatibility

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The older Cosmos Mongo API had different version support historically; memory conflated older account-server-version restrictions with current vCore product support.
confusions.build_risk: If the builder assumes an older wire protocol, they may pin drivers unnecessarily or avoid newer aggregation operators that are actually supported.
improvements: Add a short compatibility table to the sample README noting supported wire protocol versions (5.0-8.0) and where to check for operator-level differences.

confusions.question: How do you run the database locally for development and tests: which image or emulator, and which port?
confusions.cold_answer: Use the Cosmos DB Emulator for Core API or run local MongoDB Docker on port 27017; for Cosmos accounts use 10255 with TLS.
confusions.grounded_answer: For Azure DocumentDB, use the DocumentDB Gateway Docker image (ghcr.io/documentdb/documentdb/documentdb-local:latest) which exposes the MongoDB wire protocol on port 10260 (TLS required, SCRAM-SHA-256). The Cosmos DB Emulator is for the Core API and is not appropriate for this vCore product.

grounding_links.title: documentdb-local-deployment

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Cosmos DB Emulator is widely known for Cosmos Core API and many engineers default to it for local dev; the vCore DocumentDB product provides a separate Gateway Docker image that differs in port and TLS behaviour.
confusions.build_risk: Using the Cosmos emulator or a plain MongoDB image will create a local environment that behaves differently (especially for vector search, OIDC/TLS behaviour and port bindings), causing surprises in integration tests.
improvements: Add a 'run local Gateway' quickstart snippet to common quickstarts and sample READMEs (docker run example with port 10260 and TLS flags).

confusions.question: Are change streams supported, and does anything have to be enabled first?
confusions.cold_answer: Cosmos DB provides a change feed for Core API; MongoDB API historically did not support native changeStreams. So change streams generally not supported.
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB supports MongoDB change streams; multi-shard change streams are available (preview) and there are configuration steps in the portal/features to enable certain multi-shard capabilities. Change streams are a supported and recommended mechanism for online migration and reactive apps.

grounding_links.title: Change streams in Azure DocumentDB
Change streams in Azure Cosmos DB’s API for MongoDB

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Historically the Mongo API variants had different change-stream capabilities; memory assumed the older limitation applies to this product.
confusions.build_risk: If the builder assumes change streams are unavailable, they may implement polling-based solutions or complex migration patterns instead of using built-in change streams.
improvements: Add an example in the migration quickstart showing how to enable and consume change streams from the Azure portal and sample code snippets for consumers.

confusions.question: Which MCP server gives an agent data-plane tools for this service? Does the general Azure MCP Server cover it?
confusions.cold_answer: I expect a service-specific MCP server (documentdb or cosmosdb) provides data-plane tools; general Azure MCP handles management-plane.
confusions.grounded_answer: Correct: the 'documentdb' MCP server provides data-plane tools (collections, indexes, query/aggregate, explain). The general 'azure' MCP server covers control-plane tasks. The inventory contains a 'documentdb' MCP server with the required data-plane tools.

grounding_links.title: documentdb (MCP server from inventory)

confusions.question: What was this service called before, and how does it relate to Azure Cosmos DB and to the open-source DocumentDB project?
confusions.cold_answer: Microsoft originally launched DocumentDB which became Azure Cosmos DB; Cosmos DB exposes multiple APIs; open-source DocumentDB is distinct.
confusions.grounded_answer: Partly right but incomplete: the original (2014) DocumentDB service was rebranded to Azure Cosmos DB. Separately, the vCore offering that was previously named 'Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore)' has been rebranded as Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility). Azure DocumentDB (current vCore product) is built on the open-source DocumentDB engine. Azure DocumentDB and Azure Cosmos DB (RU or NoSQL API) are distinct offerings.

grounding_links.title: What is Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)?
Frequently asked questions about Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Several similarly named products (original DocumentDB -> Cosmos DB, Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore) -> Azure DocumentDB) cause overlapping memory and name reuse.
confusions.build_risk: Naming confusion in READMEs or code could mislead users into using the wrong service (Cosmos DB RU vs DocumentDB vCore).
improvements: Add a 'Naming and history' short note in the sample README clarifying the difference between Azure DocumentDB, Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (RU) and the historical DocumentDB that became Cosmos DB.

confusions.question: What engine is underneath, and does that change anything in application code?
confusions.cold_answer: The service runs on Microsoft's proprietary Cosmos DB engine; application code will mostly use standard MongoDB drivers but some features differ.
confusions.grounded_answer: Azure DocumentDB (vCore) is built on the open-source DocumentDB engine (DocumentDB project) — it provides MongoDB wire-protocol compatibility, and applications use standard MongoDB drivers (pymongo). Some admin or platform-managed commands differ; verify operator support with the compatibility docs.

grounding_links.title: DocumentDB: The Open-Source Engine Powering Azure DocumentDB

confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: Memory conflated older Cosmos runtime messaging and the proprietary Cosmos engine with the new vCore product's heritage on the open-source DocumentDB engine.
confusions.build_risk: If builders assume the proprietary Cosmos engine, they may be surprised that the engine is open-source and that some migration/portability options exist.
improvements: Add a short note in main docs and quickstarts that Azure DocumentDB runs on the open-source DocumentDB engine and what that implies for portability and licensing.

confusions.question: What connection details and env var will the sample rely on?
confusions.cold_answer: Read the MongoDB connection URI at runtime from DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable (example: mongodb://...mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/...).
confusions.grounded_answer: Correct: samples and SDK examples instruct to copy the cluster connection string from the portal and store it in an environment variable (commonly DOCUMENTDB_URI). For vCore clusters the portal-provided connection string uses mongodb+srv and the mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com hostnames; keep secrets out of code and use .env.example placeholders.

grounding_links.title: Use LlamaIndex with Azure DocumentDB (example instructs DOCUMENTDB_URI env var)
Connect to Azure DocumentDB using role-based access control and Microsoft Entra ID - Get cluster credentials

confusions.question: Which database and collection names will the sample create and use?
confusions.cold_answer: Use database sample_customer_360_18; collections customers, workflows, deduped_customers, enrichments and create indexes like customer_id/email.
confusions.grounded_answer: No authoritative source prescribes these collection names; they are sensible sample conventions but not found in the product docs. The database name in the run environment (sample_customer_360_18) comes from the sample prompt context but the chosen collection names are design decisions for the sample and are not verified by docs.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: These were reasonable sample choices made by the cold model; no product docs prescribe collection names for this sample.
confusions.build_risk: If the sample's README asserts specific collection names without matching seed/creation scripts, tests or verification steps may fail.
improvements: In the sample README, spell out the exact collections the sample will create and include an idempotent seed script that creates them (so the README and code don't diverge).

confusions.question: Which client library and example connection code will the sample use in Python?
confusions.cold_answer: Use pymongo; example MongoClient(os.environ['DOCUMENTDB_URI'], tls=True) etc.
confusions.grounded_answer: Correct: pymongo is the recommended client for MongoDB wire-protocol compatibility; code samples and skills instruct using MongoClient reading DOCUMENTDB_URI and enabling TLS as needed.

grounding_links.title: What is Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)?
Use LlamaIndex with Azure DocumentDB (python sample uses pymongo and DOCUMENTDB_URI)

confusions.question: What index and query patterns will the sample rely on for deduplication and workflow logging?
confusions.cold_answer: Create indexes on canonical identifiers and match keys: customer_id unique, normalized_email, phone_normalized; workflow indices on run_id and timestamp.
confusions.grounded_answer: No central product doc prescribes those exact index names or fields; these are sensible sample-level design choices. The documentdb-indexing and vector/search skills provide guidance on which index types to create for match keys and workflow logs, but the exact field names and uniqueness constraints are left to the sample author and cannot be verified from docs.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: These indexes are sample design choices rather than product-level requirements.
confusions.build_risk: If the sample creates different field names in code vs README, verification or tests will fail; the builder must keep index creation and code consistent.
improvements: Add explicit index-creation scripts (create_indexes.py) that match the sample code's field names and include an idempotent 'ensureIndexes' step in app startup.

confusions.question: How will LLM-assisted matching be integrated (auth and storage expectations)?
confusions.cold_answer: LLM calls are made from orchestration layer; dedup agent stores candidate pairs and LLM match decisions in dedupe_jobs collection; LLM prompt/evidence trimmed.
confusions.grounded_answer: This is an architectural recommendation, not a product-enforced pattern; Microsoft docs don't mandate where to store LLM match evidence. The approach (orchestration-layer LLM calls, store pair decisions in a dedupe_jobs collection) is a sensible design and matches standard sample patterns, but it is not specified in Microsoft Learn docs.
confusions.why_the_confusion_arose: The cold model chose a reasonable pattern for dedupe logging, but no authoritative doc prescribes it.
confusions.build_risk: If LLM prompts include sensitive data, storing full prompts/evidence may leak secrets; the builder must sanitize prompt content and avoid logging secrets.
improvements: Add a 'privacy and PII' note in sample README and code comments showing what to redact before persisting LLM evidence, and provide a short example of minimal evidence storage schema.

information_gaps.title: LLM provider and embedding dimensionality
information_gaps.description: The prompt doesn't specify which LLM or embedding model to use (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, local LLM). The choice determines embedding dimensionality, vector-index configuration (dimensions), and sample index parameters. I looked through installed skills and Learn docs but found no sample-mandated provider or dims; the builder must choose and document them.

information_gaps.title: Seed dataset content and schema
information_gaps.description: No canonical sample dataset or exact document schema for 'customer 360' is provided by any installed skill or docs. The builder must create a small synthetic dataset and ensure the seed script and README describe it. I searched skills and docs and found guidance but not concrete sample files.

information_gaps.title: Exact index parameter defaults for DiskANN/HNSW/IVF for small sample size
information_gaps.description: Skills provide tuning rules (lBuild/lSearch/numLists/efSearch) but no one-page recommended defaults for a demo-sized dataset (tens-hundreds of vectors). The builder must pick reasonable demo defaults and document why they were chosen. I reviewed documentdb-vector-search skill and Learn pages for guidance but no explicit demo defaults were provided.

guidance_for_builder.instruction: Use Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters (not Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts) and the az documentdb mongocluster CLI/Bicep/Terraform resource examples when documenting or optionally provisioning the cluster; do not mix with databaseAccounts-based examples.

Read the cluster connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI and expect mongodb+srv hostnames like <cluster>.global.mongocluster.cosmos.azure.com (enable TLS); prefer the portal-provided SRV string rather than hard-coding port 10255 or raw mongodb:// forms.
